chunks: Al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad and another, from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn al-ʿAbbās ibn ʿĀmir, from Mūsā ibn Hilāl al-Kindī, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAṭāʾ, from Abī Jaʿfar (عليه السلام), who said:
I said to him: Indeed, your Shiʿah in al-ʿIrāq are many. By Allah, there is none like you among your Ahl al-Bayt, so how is it that you do not rise?
He said: O ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAṭāʾ, you have begun spreading your ears for the foolish. Yes, by Allah, I am not your Sahib.
He said: I said to him, Then who is our Sahib? He said: Look for the one whose birth is hidden from the people; that one is your Sahib.
Indeed, there is no one from us who is pointed at by fingers and chewed by tongues except that he dies in rage or is humiliated.

key_terms.تَخْرُجُ: you rise or come out in open revolt
key_terms.شِيعَتَكَ: your Shiʿah, your followers and loyal adherents
key_terms.صَاحِبِكُمْ: your Sahib, the awaited master or leader
key_terms.يُشَارُ إِلَيْهِ بِالْإِصْبَعِ: being publicly identified and singled out
key_terms.يُمْضَغُ بِالْأَلْسُنِ: being talked about repeatedly by people

ai.seo_question: How does al-Kafi describe the hidden birth of the awaited Sahib from Ahl al-Bayt?
ai.summary: This hadith records Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام) denying that he is the awaited Sahib and directing attention instead to one whose birth would be concealed from the people. It highlights the theme of ghaybah (occultation) and indicates that the true Qa'im from the Ahl al-Bayt would not be publicly identifiable in the ordinary way.
